reason_for_v1: V0 was preregistered with n up to 22 and an independent fresh exact oracle after every effective update, but the current Python runtime hit its hard execution timeout before completing the n=18 cells. No V0 performance output is reused. V1 is a new, outcome-aware follow-up that preserves the exact per-update oracle and strategy definitions while limiting the holdout to sizes that fit the observed runtime envelope.

holdout.game: generated monotone simple game from subset-minimal random supports using the same generator family as prior incremental holdout
holdout.observation_stream: seeded sample without replacement from all coalitions

strategies.always_incremental: Conjoin only newly strengthening boundary clauses into one persistent ROBDD; never rebuild.
strategies.always_rebuild: After every effective boundary update, fresh-rebuild from the current reduced boundary before rank evaluation.
strategies.periodic_32: Incremental updates with fresh rebuild after every 32 effective boundary changes since last rebuild.
strategies.ratio_4: Incremental updates; rebuild when allocated_nonterminal_nodes / max(1, reachable_live_nonterminal_nodes) >= 4 after an effective update.
strategies.hybrid_ratio4_or_64: Incremental updates; rebuild when allocation/live >=4 or 64 effective updates since last rebuild.

correctness_oracle: At every effective boundary update, independently fresh-rebuild from the reduced boundary and require exact equality of the full rank-count vector for every strategy. Oracle time excluded from strategy runtime.

primary: nonterminal node allocations created by strategy managers
memory_proxy: maximum allocated/live ratio observed before optional rebuild
maximum allocated nonterminals in current manager
cost_accounting.reporting: Runtime and memory proxies remain separate; no after-the-fact scalarization.

resource_guard.on_limit: no partial result may be treated as a completed cell or reused as performance evidence

predeclared_tests: Zero exact-rank mismatches are required for every completed strategy cell.
Compare trigger strategies with always_incremental and always_rebuild on both runtime and max allocated/live ratio.
Call a trigger useful only when it reduces a memory proxy relative to always_incremental at finite explicitly reported runtime overhead, or reduces runtime at no worse memory proxy.
Report if ratio_4 never fires on this size range; absence of firing is evidence only for these streams.
Do not infer asymptotic complexity or applicability to nonmonotone real proof utility.
scope: Twelve newly seeded small monotone-game streams chosen after V0 timed out; V1 conclusions cannot be back-projected onto the unfinished V0 larger sizes.
